The Republic of Dawn Bringer

The Republic of Dawn Bringer was founded under the the leadership of Igon Dawn Bringer who was known for slaying the first dragon Soriel the Great who threatened the region with her strategic strikes on leaders in the region. The republic of Dawn Bringer has fought dragons for centuries trying to expand their lands and protect their capital city of Dawn Bringer from dragon attacks. Under Igon The Republic of Dawn Bringer prospered and the dragons were forced off the continent of Dominia into the lands of Aeternus. Igon would set up a monarch who was elected by the people. This monarch would then promote certain people to positions in the government. Igon would open relations with the empire of Certa who would connect his nation with the rest of the continent. Igon would have two sons Romulus and Giaus who were trained by Igon's two commanders of the Dawn Bringer army. These two commanders were Cornelius and Julius and played major roles in both Igon’s sons lives as well as public life. Towards the later years of Igon’s life the grip on his land waned and boarder disputes with the empire of Certa did not go well under his watch. Igon was known for his prowess in battle not his negotiation skills at the table. Igon would die of old age and his son Romulus would be elected monarch after his demise. Romulus would immediately appoint Giaus to a governors role within the republic.
During Romulus’s rein Juilus would die preventing a coup attempting to take Romulus’s life. Immediately Giaus was appointed to take Juilus’s position as commander of the army. This established the first archduke of the army which was a ceremonial role meant to delegate diplomatic responsibilities as well as daily government responsibilities during times of war. During this time the empire of Certa shared its goal of sharing the continent between three nations, The Republic of Dawn Bringer, Citadel of the Light, and The Certa empire. Romulus looking to claim more land for his people told them he would consider their offer. Weeks later the diplomatic relations between Axeland and the republic broke down and Romulus agreed to join the Certa empire. At this time Ajunta Pall the leader of the Axelands controlled most of the land between the Certa empire and the Axelands with a small portion to the west controlled by the Citadel of the Light. After Axeland cut ties with The republic of Dawn Bringer, Romulus joined the empire of Certa along with the Citadel of the light to create the Grand Holy Alliance (GHA). With Romulus at war Gaius took on the responsibilities of running the nation and became wildly popular among the public. During the height of Gaius’s power he separated the power of the government and military and introduced the worship of the Certa as the states faith. This tied the people of the Republic of Dawn Bringer closer to the Certa empire. Meanwhile Romulus pushed Ajunta Pall back to the Axelands with the help of the GHA. Romulus would hand the war effort over to Dominicus as he longed to return to his homeland and be with his people. Ajunta Pall would launch a counter ambush from the sea and push Dominicus back cutting off the Citadel of Light from the GHA.
Romulus would send aid with Dominicus’s counter attack to free them but would not go himself because he was needed in the north near the capital of Dawn Bringer. Upon Romulus’s return he entered the city of Dawn Bringer a hero and witnessed the massive changes Gaius made in his absence. Romulus would proceed to congratulate his brother on his popularity and updated him on the war efforts as communicating with the republic was inconvenient at this time in history. Romulus would proceed to lose the election for monarch to Gaius who would then appoint Romulus as Archcommander of the armies of Dawn Bringer. During Gaius’s term he would get rid of the title of monarch and replace it with the title of Archduke. This clearly separated the sphere of war from the sphere of the state. Gaius faced many challenges throughout his term as Archduke of Dawn Bringer like the return of the dragons and the defeat of the GHA in the Axelands during the first continental war. With the empire of Certa shattered due to Dominicus’s death (leader of the Certa empire) and the GHA’s defeat at Korriban, Romulus was forced to take up the head of the GHA and was slowly pushed back to a stand still at the boarder of the Certa empire where peace was made and no gains were made. At this point in time Romulus traveled up north to repel the dragon invasion from Aeternus with the elite special forces of the army of Dawn Bringer.
He would successfully repel the first wave of dragons but had no effective way to cross the seas and enter Aeternus. Romulus died on the battlefield in the battle of Draconis at the norther boarder of the Republic  here the sea separates the continent of Dominia from Aeternus. The King of Dragons Rex Draco defeated Romulus in battle but was gravely wounded in the process and forced to retreat. Romulus’s remains were brought back to the capital where a memorial and feast was held in his honor. After peace was established with the Axelands the empire of Certa split into two entities the Union of Certa and the empire of Certa. The Republic of Dawn Bringer aligned more closely to the empire over the union. A year after romulus’s death a suitable archcommander was still not found and the army was directionless. On the celebration day of the Republic of Dawn Bringers founding Gaius was assassinated with a dagger. The killer was never found and an election was held to replace Gaius. His predecessor was his daughter Aurora who was elected the next Archduchess but was unpopular among the people due to her unpreparedness for office and poor handling of the second continental war. Aurora was eager to take attention away from her fathers death and used the second continental war as an excuse to make a statement of power in her fathers name. It is said that Aurora was effective in coordinating attacks with the certa empire at the beginning of the war but was forced to pull some of her forces away from the war to deal with dragons in the north. This is the reason the forces of Dawn Bringer were less in number at the siege of Korriban and the final battle at Iron Root. An Archduke would never be looked upon as favorable as Gaius was. In the preceding years Archdukes would struggle to meet the peoples needs and constantly be replaced.
That is until Bismarck a commoner was elected to the position of Archduke. He provided a sense of unity around the military and modernized the military to keep up with current times as centuries had passed by this point and Dawn Bringer was undeveloped compared to other nations. Bismarck would reduce the influence of the nobility without totally destroying it. Bismarck would turn Dawn Bringer and its army from one of the most vulnerable cities to one of the strongest powers on the continent. Bismarck also distanced his nation from the GHA but still remained amenable to this old alliance. After Bismarck died in his sleep at the age of one hundred the current Archduke would come to power Constance. She would keep the status quo in the republic while pursuing interests outside of her nation. Constance is a big supporter of RavensWood Bluff for unknown reasons.

Born as Korran of the Stonebound, Solskar was once a proud soldier serving under the Republic of Dawn Bringer’s frontier command. Young Korran was ordered by a Dawn Bringer commander to raid a supposed cult of dragon-worshippers hiding in the north. He led the raid, burning the "cultists" village and struck them down, leaving no survivors. The “cult” turned out to be peaceful refugees from Aeternus who followed a gentler, older form of the Light. Soon enough, he began to discover the truth; he realized the villagers had not served dragons, but the Light in an older, purer form. Amid the ashes, he found a golden relic and lifted it toward the dawn in remorse. It flared violently, searing a scar of living light across his chest. 

His commander called it blasphemy. Korran was left to die in the ashes, his wound burning like the sun. Somehow, he crawled from the ash months later, the Light still glowing beneath his skin. He took the name Solskar, “the wound of the sun”, and disappeared into the wilderness. For years, he had wandered the borderlands between the Republic and the Aeternian wastes. He earned little and helped those that he could, in hopes of one day atoning for his sins.
_ 
His wandering eventually led him deep into the northern wilds, where the Republic’s reach had long since faded. There, hidden beneath the frost and stone, he found the ruins of an old temple swallowed by vines. Its carvings did not bear the sun of Certa, but a circle of light surrounded by roots and flowers. Inside, a faint warmth pulsed from beneath the earth, the same hue as the scar across his chest. Solskar knelt in silence, not asking for forgiveness, but simply to listen. He listened to the wind, the rustle of leaves, and the quiet songs of nature. And, for the first time, he felt peace instead of pain.

He realized then that the Light was not meant to burn, but to nurture and preserve. Solskar swore an oath to protect the lives of those who struggle to endure in the shadows. When he left the temple, his scar no longer seared; it glowed softly, like sunlight through the trees.

The Holy Crown

Wondrous Item (headgear), Very Rare (requires attunement by a Monk or Cleric)

This delicate circlet is forged from pale gold and inlaid with tiny shards of crystal that emit a faint, constant light. The inner surface is etched with prayers in Celestial that shift when read, sometimes whispering in a language you almost understand. The air around the circlet appears to resonate with a calm, serene energy.

When worn, the air around the bearer feels calm, and even in chaos, their heart beats steady and sure. The bearer is immune to being frightened.

Divine Focus

While wearing the Holy Crown, you gain a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws against spells.

In addition, when you make a Wisdom (Insight) or Wisdom (Perception) check, you can add your proficiency bonus twice instead of once (you must already be proficient in the skill).

Radiant Strikes

Your unarmed strikes count as magical and deal an extra 1d6 radiant damage.
If you already have the Ki-Empowered Strikes feature, you can instead empower one strike per turn with divine light, dealing an additional 1d10 radiant damage.

Aura of Serenity

As an action, you can release a wave of tranquil, divine energy from the crown. Each creature of your choice within 20 feet must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier).
On a failed save, a creature is charmed by you until the end of your next turn and can’t take hostile actions. On a success, it is instead calmed — the first time it would make an attack before the end of its next turn, it must roll a d6; on a 1–3, the attack automatically misses.

You can use this property once per short or long rest.

Channel Divinity: Perfect Form

If you spend 4 Ki points (no action required), you can activate this divine channel for 1 minute. During this time:

You gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

You can move across liquids and vertical surfaces without falling.

Your melee attacks shed bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for another 10 feet.
You heal 1d4 hp at the end of each turn.

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

Curse: Burden of Purity

The Crown’s blessing demands inner balance. If you willingly perform an act of cruelty or deceit, the Crown’s light dims and turns cold.

You lose all benefits of the item until you meditate in prayer for 1 hour and succeed on a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw.

Failing the saving throw imposes one level of exhaustion as divine energy scorches your mind.

Pronunciation of sounds in Orothuun (language of Solskar's tribe)

a = ah (as in fAther)

e = eh (bEd)

i = ee (machIne)

o = oh (stOne)

u = oo (rUle)

uu = extended / sacred emphasis

th = soft (thin)

r = lightly rolled (optional)

Words flow in 2–3 syllables typically
Sentence Structure
Subject – Verb – Concept

Example:

Solskar varun suun.
(Solskar meets the wound.)

Abstract statements can drop the subject:

(Suur) varun ei suun.
(Light meets the wound.)
Example Roots

Orothuun – oath speech / sacred tongue
Varun – to meet / to align
Suun – wound / inner scar
Suur – light (pure light, not fire)
Norath – endure / stand firm
Vel – whole / restored
Ei – the / that (linking particle)
Thalen – people / kin
Moruun – shadow / absence
Kael – path / journey
Common Phrases
Varun ei suun.
Light meets the wound. 

Suur norath.
Light endures. 

Kael vel.
